selection.reason: North Carolina was the highest-ranked state outside the existing queue with a bounded official source family: state-designated paddle trails, public boating accesses, and a deep active USGS discharge network. The Roanoke River State Trail supplied the first corridor-first window.

reviewStrategy.description: Use provider-baseline gauge review for durable dispositions, but keep discovery open: independently sweep official and partner access networks, map them to direct live gauges, screen at most three same-family candidates, and deeply research at most the strongest survivor. Keep stage-only gauges visible as deferred blockers rather than inventing route thresholds.

completedWindows.outcome: Published the 6-mile Gaston/Roanoke Rapids Access to Weldon Outtake segment on direct USGS 02080500 using the Roanoke River State Trail, Roanoke River Partners, Dominion Energy release guidance, and a canonical NHD geometry. Deferred the two stage-only downstream gauges because no station-specific paddling threshold supports distinct routes.

Published the 6.8-mile Ronda Park to Crater Park in Elkin segment on direct USGS 02112250 using the Yadkin River State Trail, Yadkin County access data, NC Wildlife access data, Elkin facility information, Yadkin Riverkeeper operating guidance, and a canonical NHD geometry. Deferred Patterson and Enon as distinct follow-up candidates because the bounded window did not complete separate endpoint and station-tied operating packages.

Published the Kerr Scott Tailwater to Smoot Park Class I–II segment on direct USGS 0211139110 using the Yadkin River State Trail designation, documented tailwater and Smoot access, Riverkeeper safety guidance, current telemetry, and a canonical NHD geometry. Deferred Wilkesboro and Yadkin College because the stronger tailwater survivor already covers the verified access chain and no additional distinct station-tied endpoint and hazard package cleared the bounded window.

Completed durable disposition of all remaining NC provider-baseline entries. No additional route was published; 278 previously unreviewed stations were marked blocked/deferred with explicit retry conditions requiring a distinct public endpoint pair, station-tied operating guidance, safety evidence, and duplicate-scope clearance.

Published the 5.5-mile Saxapahaw Mill Race to Union Bridge intermediate Haw River Paddle Trail segment on direct USGS 02096500 after verifying the named public endpoint pair, section-specific 2.1–4.0 ft planning band, live telemetry, safety/dam notes, duplicate scope, and canonical NHD geometry. Deferred the Bynum and Reedy Fork candidates because they do not yet have a distinct complete route package.

Published the 10-mile advanced Anglin Mill / Mayo Beach to Business 220 Mayo River run on direct USGS 02070500 after verifying named public endpoints, station-tied 150/250/1,000 cfs planning cues, Boiling Hole and mandatory pre-dam take-out hazards, duplicate scope, and canonical NHD geometry. Deferred the Dan and French Broad candidates for separate route packages.

Published the approximately 5.9-mile Hanging Rock to Moratock Park Class I–II Dan River section on direct USGS 02071000 after verifying the named public endpoint pair, local 150/250/1,000 cfs planning cues, access and moving-water safety notes, duplicate scope, and canonical NHD geometry. Deferred French Broad and New River candidates for separate route packages.

Published the approximately 5.5-mile Pisgah Forest to Penrose French Broad Paddle Trail section on direct USGS 03439000 after verifying named public accesses currently listed open, numeric local flow guidance, obstruction/recovery checks, duplicate scope, and canonical NHD geometry. Deferred New River and Neuse candidates for separate route packages.

Published the 4.7-mile Falls Dam Tailrace to Thornton Road Neuse River section on direct USGS 02087183 after verifying Raleigh's named public paddle-launch chain, official 200 cfs slow-float cue, current Thornton nonmotorized launch notice, downstream closure context, duplicate scope, and canonical NHD geometry. Deferred New River and Lumber because a station-tied section threshold and complete access package still require confirmation.

Completed the final New River/Lumber access-first audit. Confirmed official endpoint networks, route mileage, park status, direct gauges, and independent paddling context, but did not publish either route because neither candidate had a defensible station-tied paddling threshold and complete operating band. Both gauges received durable deferred dispositions with explicit retry conditions; no additional NC route cleared the publication bar in this methodology window.

Published new-river-todd-wagoner after independently verifying Todd Island Park and Wagoner public canoe-access anchors, the seven-mile Class II section, an informational 100–2,500 cfs same-river proxy band, park camping posture, safety caveats, approved context imagery, access controls, and canonical geometry.

Published cape-fear-river-raven-rock-lillington after verifying NCWRC public access anchors, the Raven Rock park no-kayak/canoe-launch caveat, the Cape Fear Class I–II hazard package, an informational 200–5,000 cfs band tied to direct Lillington telemetry, separate Canoe Camp posture, rights-clean same-river imagery, access controls, and canonical geometry. The source’s eight-mile label conflicts with a 9.1-mile straight-line endpoint separation, so the app uses an explicit conservative approximately ten-mile planning label.

Published tuckasegee-river-dillsboro-barkers-creek after verifying the five-mile Class II section, NCWRC C.J. Harris and Barker’s Creek public accesses, direct Barker’s Creek telemetry, an informational 500–2,500 cfs band, regulated-release and Dillsboro dam hazards, no endpoint camping claim, rights-clean same-river imagery, access controls, and canonical geometry.

Published valley-river-andrews-tomotla after verifying NCWRC Andrews/Valley River canoe access, the named Class I Andrews-to-Tomotla/Murphy section, direct Tomotla telemetry, an informational 60–1,000 cfs band, explicit low-water/strainer/wire and lower-landing caveats, no endpoint camping claim, rights-clean same-river imagery, access controls, and canonical geometry. The source’s eight-mile label conflicts with a 10.5-mile straight-line endpoint separation, so the app uses an explicit conservative approximately eleven-mile planning label.

independentDiscovery.method: Access-first regional water-trail sweep independent of the provider-baseline gauge-ledger order
independentDiscovery.finding: The statewide completion sweep was independently stress-tested with an access-first regional water-trail method. That reopened pass added Haw, Mayo, Dan, French Broad, and Neuse routes. The continuation pass then added bounded New River, Cape Fear, and Tuckasegee sections with explicit proxy/access-anchor or source-distance caveats. Additional New River, Lumber, Smith, Deep, lower Neuse, and other candidates remain explicit retryable deferrals rather than invented score bands.

validation.notes: All 288 NC inventory entries have durable covered, blocked, or deferred dispositions. Haw window 05, Mayo window 06, Dan window 07, French Broad window 08, and Neuse window 09 passed route, gauge, safety, geometry, access-registry, and rollback checks. Final window 10 screened New River and Lumber and retained both as retryable threshold gaps. The five added routes remain reversible by removing the NC route and trip-detail files, their registry entries, route-scoped geometries, and linked operational records without touching prior state work.
